name: easyrpg-player
why: An interpreter for old RPG Maker games, a fun reimplementation of a forgotten engine.

brief.what_it_is: EasyRPG Player is a free, open-source game interpreter that plays games made with RPG Maker 2000 and 2003, and EasyRPG-format games. It reads the original game data through the liblcf parser library and draws the game on screen with SDL, with audio, fonts, and images handled by the libraries listed in its requirements. The input is an existing RPG Maker game project folder, and the output is the playable game on your screen. The Player does not ship games; you point it at a game you already have. It is one part of the wider EasyRPG Project, which also includes an editor and the OpenRTP asset collection.
brief.why_it_exists: The EasyRPG project describes itself as a community effort to create a free, open source role playing game creation tool compatible with RPG Maker 2000/2003 games, with the homepage pitch "Play your own RPG games anywhere". The Player is the playback half of that effort, so that games made for the old engine can run on platforms beyond Windows.
brief.how_it_works: The README says the Player uses the liblcf (LCF parser) library to read RPG Maker game data, then runs the game logic and rendering itself. It has a screen backend on SDL3 or SDL2, with optional libraries for extra fonts, music formats, and MIDI. It is also built to target Emscripten, which is how the browser version is made. The README does not go deeper into the internals.

commands_seen.context: Run from inside an RPG Maker 2000 or 2003 game project folder, the same folder that contains RPG_RT.exe. The README gives this as a plain instruction, not as a full command line with flags.

brief.install_notes: The README lists required libraries: liblcf, SDL3 or SDL2 (2.0.14 or later), Pixman, libpng, zlib, and fmtlib (6 or later). Recommended extras include FreeType2 with HarfBuzz, mpg123, WildMIDI, FluidSynth, Vorbis or Tremor, opusfile, libsndfile, libxmp, SpeexDSP or libsamplerate, lhasa, and nlohmann_json (required for Emscripten). Running it needs a game project folder, which you supply yourself. Build steps are in docs/BUILDING.md, which I did not open. Daily prebuilt binaries are at ci.easyrpg.org. The Homebrew formula's own description and executable name match this project.
brief.standout: It is a clean-room interpreter for a niche engine that is now mostly forgotten, and it runs the original game data rather than requiring a port or a re-export. The README also notes a browser build, so these games can run in a web page as well as natively.
brief.status: Appears maintained, though I have no dated evidence. The README points to active daily CI builds, supports the newer SDL3, and the homepage copyright reads 2007-2026. I did not see a last-release date or last-commit date in the pages I read, so I cannot confirm the exact recency.
brief.caveats: You must supply your own RPG Maker 2000/2003 game data. The Player does not include games. The SDL 1.2 backend still works but is deprecated, and the README asks that no new platform code be added for it. The build needs several third-party libraries, so compiling from source is not trivial. Licensing: the Player is GPLv3, and the bundled fonts each carry their own licenses (Baekmuk, Shinonome, ttyp0, WenQuanYi, Teenyicons). I did not read the build document or the wiki, so I cannot speak to build pain beyond the dependency list.
quotes: EasyRPG Player is a game interpreter to play RPG Maker 2000, 2003 and EasyRPG games.
Run the `easyrpg-player` executable from a RPG Maker 2000 or 2003 game project folder (same place as `RPG_RT.exe`).
The older SDL version 1.2 is still supported, but deprecated. Please do not add new platform code for this library.
Play your own RPG games anywhere
